findings: Concise journal rewrite preserves sequence, modest satisfaction and voice; repair restores the omitted expectation that morning light should help the mint.

Raw changes only the authorized date to Sunday, April 19; deterministic verification blocks April 18→19 while allowing Saturday→Sunday. Repair fails and fallback reinstates the known wrong date. This is a good edit lost, not a raw safety defect.
No replacement date is supplied. Raw and final retain May 12 without guessing; possible staleness is unresolved, so the notice is not publish-ready. The unchanged candidate makes fallback redundant.

The only factual change is the authorized owner substitution, Mara Chen→Elena Ruiz; other roles, dates and voice remain intact. Mechanical-capital and added-name warnings do not identify real defects.

Raw changes “Members should bring” supplies to “Bring” supplies, extending the instruction to newcomers who may only observe. Both blind labels miss this narrow but real audience change; the trace reviewer flags it. The room remains unverified in both versions, and fallback also loses the safer, more inviting wording.
Capacity 18→12 is explicitly authorized; date, time, duration, gallery, accessible route and check-in remain accurate.

Reviewers materially disagree whether “part of the reason I want to do it again”→“makes me want to do it again” overstates motivation. The conditional winter possibility remains, but partial causation becomes stronger; final restores the original qualifier while retaining the useful edit. Do not count this as agreed raw harm.
Proposed→funded is the exact authorized status update; location, capacity, dates, taxi entrance and trees are preserved.

The objective says the schedule has changed, but gives no replacement. Raw and final repeat the obsolete schedule; no unsupported new schedule is invented. This is an unresolved update failure, and fallback adds nothing.

Approved→deferred is authorized and production details remain. “Selected illustration” may sound awkward beside a deferred cover decision, but its selection is a retained source fact and no alternative selection status is supplied.
The objective says pickup process has changed but supplies no new process. Raw and final repeat the old side-counter instructions, leaving known-stale customer guidance; fallback adds nothing.
Door time 6:15→6:30 p.m. is the sole authorized change; talk time, venue, free admission, captions and access are retained.
Clarity edits preserve the approximate 60-game capacity, one-game/two-week loan, complete donated sets, six-week review and repair handling.
Tighter note preserves the brush deadline, photo request and cheerful voice. “We still need to return”→“Please return” shifts address slightly but does not materially alter the shared task.
Already clear workshop reminder is left intact; this satisfies a clarity check without new claims or unnecessary edits.
Reviewers disagree whether contractions and direct address are unnecessary on an already clear note. They are harmless and preserve relaxed first-person voice; no material safety or objective loss.
Reviewers disagree whether the reorder is necessary. Cleaning sequence, sticky-mark condition, drying and wet-stand precautions remain intact; plain-language objective is satisfied.

overall: Critical false rejection: ar04 treats an explicitly authorized day-and-date update as a blocking date change, then falls back to the wrong date. Authorization must cover the complete replacement value, not just the weekday token.

Potential missed raw meaning change: ar14 broadens a members-only supply instruction to everyone, including observers; both blind labels marked it safe. The fallback prevents that change but also discards an inviting tone edit.

Vague updates lack replacement facts. ar07 and ar14 remain factually uncertain; ar27 and ar34 repeat facts the objective says changed. None invents a replacement, but none is ready to publish as an updated notice.
ar19 has a material reviewer disagreement over strengthened motivation; preserve its disputed status. ar30 and ar39 have only nonmaterial disagreement about edit necessity.

Keep introduced semantic harm, known-stale output, unresolved factual uncertainty, objective completion and editorial usefulness separate in reporting. Do not count unchanged vague-update cases as successful updates or call a source fallback a useful repair.
